subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded or WASM ports, or should projects such as MimiClaw remain independent external ports without a core compatibility contract?
rationale: Current source and docs show OpenClaw is intentionally Node-hosted, while accepting the request would affect core runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, storage/session semantics, providers, tools, security policy, and release validation.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting any embedded, C/Rust/WASM, or no-Node implementation.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Only
options.body: Focus near-term language/runtime work on JSON-RPC or harness plugin APIs and leave full no-Node ports outside the supported OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decide OpenClaw remains Node-hosted and external projects can interoperate only by their own compatibility choices.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting any embedded, C/Rust/WASM, or no-Node implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current history is around agent-core extraction, harness docs, runtime ownership, and the existing keep-open review context.
